translations.text: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s brother, who was younger than he was, captured it, and Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah as his wife.

The descendants of Hobab the Kenite, Moses’ father-in-law, went up from the City of Palms with the people of Judah into the wilderness of Judah, which is south of Judah, near the slope of Arad. They went and settled among the people.

Manasseh did not take possession of Beth-shean, which is Scythopolis, or its dependent towns or its fields, or Taanach and its dependent towns, or the inhabitants of Dor, those living around it, and its dependent towns, or the inhabitants of Balak, those living around it, and its dependent towns, or the inhabitants of Ibleam, those living around it, and its dependent towns. The Canaanites began to dwell in that land.

They abandoned the Lord, the God of their ancestors, who had brought them out of the land of the Egyptians. They followed foreign gods, the gods of the nations around them, and bowed down to them, provoking the Lord to anger.
He gathered all the Ammonites and Amalek against them, went and defeated Israel, and took possession of the City of Palms.
He went out onto the porch, passed through the latticework, closed the doors of the upper room behind him, and bolted them.
The Israelites again did evil before the Lord, and Shamgar died.

Deborah said to him, “I will certainly go with you, but know that the honor will not be yours on the journey you are taking, for the Lord will deliver Sisera into the hands of a woman.” Deborah arose and went with Barak to Kedesh.
Jael came out to meet Sisera and said to him, “Turn aside to me, my lord, turn aside, and do not be afraid.” He turned aside to her into the tent, and she covered him with its flaps.
The mountains shook before the Lord [?] of Sinai, before the Lord, the God of Israel.
The commanders of Issachar were with Deborah and with Barak, and then Barak stretched out his feet into the valleys. Among the divisions of Reuben there were great searchings of heart.
Kings came and fought; then the kings of the Canaanites were hard pressed at Taanach, by the waters of Megiddo. I took no silver as plunder.
The Israelites did evil before the Lord, and the Lord delivered them into the hands of Midian for seven years.
The men of the city said to Joash, “Bring your son out, and let him die, because he demolished the altar of Baal and cut down the sacred grove beside it.”

The Lord said to him, “Speak in the hearing of the people and say, ‘Whoever is fainthearted, let him turn back.’” They set off from Mount Gilead, and twenty-two thousand returned from the army, while ten thousand remained.

He brought the army down to the water, and the Lord said to Gideon, “Everyone who laps the water with his tongue like a dog, set them apart; and everyone who falls to his knees to drink, set them separately.”
Gideon came to the Jordan and crossed over, he and the three hundred men with him, exhausted and hungry.
They showed no kindness to the household of Jerubbaal, who is Gideon, in return for all the good he had done for Israel.
Abimelech stayed at Arumah, and Zebul drove out Gaal and his brothers so that they could no longer live in Shechem.
Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, “Did you not hate me, drive me out of my father’s house, and send me away from you? Why have you now come to me when you are in distress?”

The king of the Ammonites said to Jephthah’s messengers, “Why did Israel take my land when it came up from Egypt, from the Arnon to the Jabbok and as far as the Jordan? Now return it to me peacefully, and I will go away.” The messengers returned to Jephthah.
But Israel traveled through the wilderness as far as the Red Sea and came to Kadesh.

Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, “Let me pass through your land.” But the king of Edom would not listen. Israel also sent to the king of Moab, but he was unwilling, and Israel remained at Kadesh.

They said to them, “Give us a sign and say, ‘Ear of grain, ear of grain.’” They could not pronounce it that way, so they seized them and slaughtered them at the fords of the Jordan. At that time forty-two thousand men of Ephraim fell.
After him, Abdon son of Hillel, the Pirathonite, judged Israel.
The angel of the Lord appeared to the woman and said to her, “Look, you are barren and have not given birth, but you will conceive and bear a son.”

When Delilah saw that he had told her everything in his heart, she sent for the rulers of the Philistines and said, “Come up this time, for he has told me everything in his heart.” All the rulers of the Philistines came up to her, bringing the silver in their hands.
They went on from there, came to the hill country of Ephraim, and reached Micah’s house.

The man got up and went after her to speak tenderly to her, reconcile her to himself, and bring her back to him. His servant was with him, along with a pair of donkeys. They went to her father’s house. When the girl’s father saw him, he came out to meet him.
The two of them sat down and ate and drank together. The girl’s father said to his son-in-law, “Now settle in here for the night, and let your heart be glad.”
But the man was unwilling to stay there overnight. He got up and left, and came to a place opposite Jebus, that is, Jerusalem. With him were a pair of saddled donkeys, and his concubine was with him.
They were opposite Jebus, and the day was far spent. The servant said to his master, “Come, let us turn aside into the city of the Jebusites and spend the night there.”
He looked up and saw the traveler in the city square. The old man said, “Where are you going, and where have you come from?”
“Here are my virgin daughter and his concubine. I will bring them outside, and you may violate them and do to them whatever pleases you. But do not do this disgraceful thing to this man.”
He said to her, “Get up, and let us go.” But she gave him no answer, for she was dead. He lifted her onto the donkey, and the man got up and went to his own home.

“But let us take ten men out of every hundred from all the tribes of Israel, a hundred out of every thousand, and a thousand out of every ten thousand, to obtain provisions for the whole army going to Gibeah of Benjamin because of all the disgraceful things they did in Israel.”
All the men of Israel, apart from the Benjaminites, passed in review: four hundred thousand men who drew the sword, all of them warriors.
The Lord defeated Benjamin before the Israelites, and that day the Israelites killed twenty-five thousand one hundred men of Benjamin, all of them men who drew the sword.
When the Benjaminites saw that they had been defeated, the men of Israel gave way to Benjamin, because they trusted in the men they had stationed in ambush around Gibeah.
The people were comforted concerning Benjamin, for the Lord had made a breach among the tribes of Israel.
